title: form.ext

toolchain.linux_packages: libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev libxdo-dev libssl-dev patchelf file

build.windows:
set "PATH=C:\Program Files\Git\bin;%PATH%"
call build_app.bat || (type build_app.log & exit /b 1)

catalog.name: form.ext
catalog.summary: The extension studio: make, preview, check, package and publish extensions for every Form app.

notes_for_owner: form.ext builds with its own build_app (macOS, Linux) and build_app.bat (Windows) in commands mode: it has no install-desktop command and its build_app takes no --config, so contract mode would stop at once. formcompiler's signing and settings reach it through src-tauri/tauri.<os>.conf.json, which Tauri merges by itself. FORMEXT_CARGO_TARGET points the Rust build at src-tauri/target (build_app's default is a cache folder outside the checkout, where the artifact globs would find nothing); --no-install keeps the macOS build from copying the app into /Applications on the runner; FORMEXT_BUNDLES adds rpm and AppImage to the Linux deb. build_app.bat freezes the engine with a bare bash, so Git Bash goes first on PATH (a bare bash can start the WSL launcher on the runner), and it writes its output only to build_app.log, so a failed Windows build prints that log. The engine is a PyInstaller one-file sidecar (binaries/formext-engine) signed by Tauri with src-tauri/entitlements.plist under the hardened runtime. macos-x64 and linux-arm64 are experimental until a first release shows the engine freezes there.
